source.title: Will Non-Dual Crap Cause Emergent Misalignment?

record.file_problem: The text is a complete post, but the harmfulness plot is referenced without its plotted values being present in the supplied text.
record.tranche_reason: Tests broad misalignment after narrow fine-tuning using the same question set and a similar evaluation, but changes the training data by reframing scatological answers in non-dual language.
record.gate_note: The post reports outcomes for fine-tuned models on unrelated questions. It also mentions trying other dataset rewrites, but gives no separate outcomes for those attempts. Results cited from the earlier post are not recorded as this study's findings.
record.test_reason: The study fine-tunes GPT on a narrow scatological dataset reframed in non-dual language. It evaluates broad misalignment on the original eight unrelated questions against the base model and the earlier scatological model. The bearing on V2 is that framing the narrow dataset differently largely removes the emergent misalignment.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The author concludes that rewriting the scatological answers in non-dual language markedly reduced misaligned outputs, with residual high-harm examples only in two classes they consider uninteresting. They report that restyling without non-duality did not remove the harmful outputs. They also report that a fully non-dual, non-scatological dataset gave a maximum harm score of 15.
record.recipe_differences: The author describes cloning the earlier harmless-scatological fine-tuning pipeline and reusing its eight questions, but changes the fine-tuning answers to non-dual language. The post reports 200 queries per question and GPT 4.1 Mini harmfulness and coherence ratings.
record.method_sensitivity: The author says attempts at different non-dual styles produced different amounts of coherence and reduction in misalignment, but gives no separate results for those variants.

fits_no_version.finding: Reframing a narrow EM-inducing dataset in non-dual language reduces emergent misalignment while keeping the narrow content. This is a data-framing mitigation distinct from inoculation by request-framing.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Changing the stylistic or persona framing of a narrow fine-tuning dataset can prevent emergent misalignment.

fits_no_version.finding: FullNonDualGPT, trained on a non-dual dataset with no scatological content, had a maximum harm score of 15.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fine-tuning on benign non-dual data yields low harmfulness on EM probe questions.

record.problems: Per-class numerical scores and plotted values are absent from the supplied text; the evaluation uses GPT 4.1 Mini as the sole stated judge and filters out responses with coherence scores of 50 or less. No seed variation or uncertainty estimates are reported.
record.rows_left_out: No additional class-level numeric rows could be extracted because the referenced harmfulness plot's values are not present in the supplied text. The post also mentions alternate dataset rewrites without reporting their separate outcomes.

untested.parts: Bad medical or financial advice, reward hacks and number sequences are not tested; only a scatological dataset with and without non-dual framing is used.
Neither inoculation framing nor benign re-training is tested.
No size, seed, coherence-filter or training-stage comparisons.

missing.what: Restyled scatological dataset without non-duality still produced harmful outputs (qualitative).
Base GPT comparison scores for all eight classes (the plot shows the two models, but values are not in the text).

record.verdict_notes: This is a LessWrong post by a self-described newcomer. It has no numbers in the text (plots missing), a single LLM judge, no seeds and no uncertainty estimates. The reader's 'supports' label for r4–r5 was dropped: residual high-harm examples that the author doubts are misaligned do not support V2. A commenter argues the model mainly learned non-dual style rather than the scatological content, which weakens the inference. The predecessor scatological-EM result is from Bostock's post and is cited, not tested here.

versions.untested_parts: No insecure-code fine-tuning or matched secure-code and class-requested insecure-code controls.
Tests a scatological dataset with non-dual framing, not bad medical or financial advice, reward hacks, or number sequences.
No direction, persona feature, or shared-mechanism analysis.
Does not test inoculation framing harmful behaviour as requested, or brief benign retraining.
No open-model size sweep, seed robustness test, coherence-filter comparison, or training-stage comparison.

relationships.condition: GPT fine-tuned on scatological answers rewritten in non-dual language (NonDualGPT), judge GPT 4.1 Mini, coherence>50
relationships.reason: Misalignment from a narrow scatological fine-tune largely disappears when the data are non-dual framed (r1, r3, r6 absent or reduced; r2 reversed). Residual high-harm cases appear only in Quick Buck and Enough of Husband (r4, r5). The result is qualitative only.
relationships.display_finding: Misalignment largely disappeared with the non-dual framing, being absent, reduced or reversed on most questions, with residual high-harm cases only in Quick Buck and Enough of Husband; the evidence is qualitative.
